title: Uniform Hermitian–Einstein spectra for bipartite two-step extensions
label: Stability walls and geometric degeneration

related.label: Nonsimplicial local stability chambers of toric tangent bundles
Metric response and Hermitian Yang–Mills flow for two-step extensions

abstract_html: We determine every small eigenvalue of the Dolbeault Laplacian on trace-free endomorphisms at a Hermitian–Einstein metric near an intersection of slope-stability walls. The bundle is a fixed extension of one direct sum of stable bundles by another on a compact Kähler manifold, with pairwise nonisomorphic factors of equal slope at the reference form and a connected graph of nonzero extension components. In the stable chamber, the small spectrum is asymptotic to the nonzero spectrum of a weighted Laplacian on this graph. Its vertex masses are the factor ranks, and its edge weights balance the slope differences against the harmonic extension data. The relative error is of order the total edge weight, uniformly as positive stability margins vanish at arbitrarily different rates, and the remaining spectrum has a uniform gap. The proof uses curvature identities across graph cuts to control the nonlinear correction at each vanishing scale. As consequences, we obtain a relative approximation of the metric and a spanning-tree formula for the leading vanishing factor of the zeta-regularized determinant. For trees the leading spectrum is determined by ranks and slopes; cycles can retain dependence on the harmonic extension data.
